I think this PR could fix most of the disk attach issue due to detach disk not succeed(could be due to many reasons), this PR could do the recover automatically, I will cherry pick the fix to all old releases.

pr_comments: hi @gnufied I followed your guidance with #55491, this PR seems not working (detach volume never happen) even it could enter into `volerr.NewDanglingError(attachErr ...`, is there sth. else I have missed?

@andyzhangx just to double check,  the volume will only be detached if another pod and comes around and tries to use it.  If no pod is attempting to use it, the volume will remain attached to the old node.  Is that what happened? 

If volume is still not detaching even if another pod tries to use it - that will be kinda weird. Can we get controller-manager logs when this happened?

I used following way to "repro" this issue:
1. attach the disk to node#A manually
2. create a pod with PVC mount which uses that disk, and that pod would run on node#B

So the disk would be detached from node#A, right? @gnufied
@andyzhangx I think so yeah. Can you post controller-manager logs with v4 verbosity?

@gnufied here is the useful logging, detach volume is skipped:

```
I0813 05:33:22.709564       1 reconciler.go:200] Cannot detach volume because it is still mounted for volume "pvc-41a31580-f5b9-4f08-b0ea-0adcba15b6db" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/azure-disk//subscriptions/b9d2281e-dcd5-4dfd-9a97-0d50377cdf76/resourceGroups/andy-mg1160alpha3/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/andy-1160alpha3-dynamic-pvc-41a31580-f5b9-4f08-b0ea-0adcba15b6db") on node "k8s-agentpool-32686255-0"
```
It's due to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/61af419d386dd9aa05ddfd6e192981ae4ab0ffc5/pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/reconciler/reconciler.go#L199-L201

At this time, the volume is in use by node#B.

And if I hack the above code by comment out the `continue` statement, it would go into 
```
I0813 06:25:46.662343       1 reconciler.go:208] RemoveVolumeFromReportAsAttached failed while removing volume "kubernetes.io/azure-disk//subscriptions/b9d2281e-dcd5-4dfd-9a97-0d50377cdf76/resourceGroups/andy-mg1160alpha3/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/andy-1160alpha3-dynamic-pvc-41a31580-f5b9-4f08-b0ea-0adcba15b6db" from node "k8s-agentpool-32686255-0" with: volume "kubernetes.io/azure-disk//subscriptions/b9d2281e-dcd5-4dfd-9a97-0d50377cdf76/resourceGroups/andy-mg1160alpha3/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/andy-1160alpha3-dynamic-pvc-41a31580-f5b9-4f08-b0ea-0adcba15b6db" does not exist in volumesToReportAsAttached list or node "k8s-agentpool-32686255-0" does not exist in nodesToUpdateStatusFor list
```

And you could find all controller manager logs here: https://gist.githubusercontent.com/andyzhangx/6d6460ad8802f78016b0b4cbce292399/raw/3ea7142feadaf8f7bb9da7c7e75016ce7559771d/controller-manager.log

okay.. so:

```
I0813 05:33:22.709564       1 reconciler.go:200] Cannot detach volume because it is still mounted for volume "pvc-41a31580-f5b9-4f08-b0ea-0adcba15b6db" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/azure-disk//subscriptions/b9d2281e-dcd5-4dfd-9a97-0d50377cdf76/resourceGroups/andy-mg1160alpha3/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/andy-1160alpha3-dynamic-pvc-41a31580-f5b9-4f08-b0ea-0adcba15b6db") on node "k8s-agentpool-32686255-0"
```

This condition will automatically go away after `maxWaitForUnmountDuration` has expired, which is fine because since we are going to detach a volume which is in "uncertain" state.

```
I0813 06:25:46.662343       1 reconciler.go:208] RemoveVolumeFromReportAsAttached failed while removing volume "kubernetes.io/azure-disk//subscriptions/b9d2281e-dcd5-4dfd-9a97-0d50377cdf76/resourceGroups/andy-mg1160alpha3/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/andy-1160alpha3-dynamic-pvc-41a31580-f5b9-4f08-b0ea-0adcba15b6db" from node "k8s-agentpool-32686255-0" with: volume "kubernetes.io/azure-disk//subscriptions/b9d2281e-dcd5-4dfd-9a97-0d50377cdf76/resourceGroups/andy-mg1160alpha3/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/andy-1160alpha3-dynamic-pvc-41a31580-f5b9-4f08-b0ea-0adcba15b6db" does not exist in volumesToReportAsAttached list or node "k8s-agentpool-32686255-0" does not exist in nodesToUpdateStatusFor list
```

I think this is a bug that you have discovered. When I made https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/78595 change - to add dangling volumes as uncertain, we stopped reporting the volume to node's status and hence it is failing. But this looks like a general problem with detaching volumes which are in uncertain state, I will open a PR to fix this. This needs better coverage to prevent regression too.

@andyzhangx actually part of my comment was not true, following error log:

```
I0813 06:25:46.662343       1 reconciler.go:208] RemoveVolumeFromReportAsAttached failed while removing volume oes not exist in nodesToUpdateStatusFor list
```

Does not stop volume from being detached - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/reconciler/reconciler.go#L208 the volume should still be detached..

> @andyzhangx actually part of my comment was not true, following error log:
> 
> ```
> I0813 06:25:46.662343       1 reconciler.go:208] RemoveVolumeFromReportAsAttached failed while removing volume oes not exist in nodesToUpdateStatusFor list
> ```
> 
> Does not stop volume from being detached - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/reconciler/reconciler.go#L208 the volume should still be detached..

@gnufied thanks a lot for your help! Finally I figured out that this is another issue in detaching disk, actually detach disk operation happens, which it could not find that disk in the list, this PR fixed these  two issues.

So this PR is ready for code review.

issue_context.title: Disks are not detached on Azure
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
Pods with PVs could not be moved from one node to another. According to the controller-manager logs, K8s tried to detach to Azure disks from the same node. One of the detach operation waited for this lock (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/azure/azure_controller_common.go#L136). While it waited for the lock, the controller-manager pod was restarted (for whatever reason, not related to this bug, lets assume an operator restarted the pod). After the restart, K8s only tried to attach the disk to the new node but is not trying to detach it first.

**What you expected to happen**:
After a restart of the controller-manager, it should continue unfinished detach operations

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
* 2 Pods with PVs running on one node
* Move both pods to another node
* restart the controller-manager shortly after the move

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.15.1
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: Azure
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:
comments:
/area provider/azure
@MSSedusch that's expected behavior, k8s controller won't continue detach volume if controller manager restarted, user needs to detach that disk volume manually.

@andyzhangx Could you please elaborate why this behaviour is expected. I would assume that the controller manager tries to reach the desired state after a restart? Then it would need to detect that the volume is still attached to the wrong node and should try to detach it once more, before it continuing to attach the (still attached) volume? This leads to many `ConflictingUserInputs` ...

Why is it required to resolve this situation by manual interaction?

I can't imagine that "manual intervention" is "desired behaviour" (yes, you wrote "expected", but that doesn't matter, if you make no proposal, how to improve this).

If this isn't fixed, we can't use Azure, period. We can't have clusters that need to be babysitted / you cannot expect people running workloads on Azure clusters and babysit them and manually fixing what should/can fix itself. Level-triggered behaviour and resilience is what made Kubernetes so successful... please bring that also to Azure's KCM/CCM.
@dkistner do you know why controller manager is restarted, it's not a common scenario, we cannot guarantee disk attach/detach functionality works if  controller manager restarted at that time.
This is an upstream issue, and there is a discussion in #81097, let's check whether we can fix it in cloud provider driver in that thread. Thanks.

I will try to fix this issue in azure disk driver, thanks all for the discussion.
details: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/80488#issuecomment-519663496
/assign

Thank you very much @andyzhangx. It means a lot to us, that there are no manual operations. I wonder how you guys deal with it in AKS, since Azure uses the same controllers, right? Anyway, it helps tremendously, that the clusters are self-healing.
@vlerenc AKS use same kube-controller-manager, while it won't be restarted easily.

OK, but how? I understand that AKS only supports 100 nodes. So, I guess you have some upper limit and just hope, nobody stresses it, because if this happens, you it either restarts or you need to scale it up and then it gets restarted as well. Also, regular maintenance, low-level as well as Kubernetes updates, all must impact it. Considering the probably thousands over thousands of clusters (I don't know, but I expect you run many), any such problem, even if unlikely by itself, must be in your interest to fix, simply because the number of clusters increases the likelihood that it happens, I would think. Anyway, thank you for making this change @andyzhangx!
@vlerenc Yes, that's reasonable, I will try to fix it as my top priority.

Is there any possible "disk.ManagedBy" is equal to "nodeName"?
